newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-WOODS HAS THE GAME FOR THE U.S. MASTERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS HAS THE GAME FOR THE U.S. MASTERS.

text.p: A buoyant Tiger Woods agreed on Tuesday he was a leading candidate to win the U.S. Masters in April at his first attempt as a professional.
The 21-year-old American, who won the Bangkok Classic by 10-shots on Sunday, was named by South African rival Ernie Els last month as the man to beat at Augusta.
Woods said his game, based around his awesome distance off the tee, was ideally suited to the Masters layout in golf's first major of the year.

"When you look at my physical aspects, I should always be favourite to win there, as should (fellow American) John Daly," Woods told reporters at a news conference before the Australian Masters tournament, starting at Huntingdale on Thursday.
"We both hit the ball long and we hit the ball very high," Woods said.
Woods won his fourth title since turning professional last August with an emphatic victory against a relatively weak field in Bangkok on Sunday.
Woods attracted huge crowds and massive media and public attention in Thailand in his first tournament as a professional in Asia.
"After what I had to go through last week, I'm not surprised by anything any more," said Woods, whose mother is a Thai. "It was very tough. Thailand was 10 times tougher than here."
Woods is being paid a reported US$300,000 to play at Huntingdale, where Australian Craig Parry will defend his title.
Tournament organisers are predicting a record crowd to follow Woods this weekend. A gallery of several thousand watched him at the pro-am warm-up event on Tuesday.
When Woods made his overseas debut as a professional at the Australian Open in Sydney last November alongside world number one Greg Norman, crowds increased 400 per cent on the previous year.
